headline: Kai, $100 oil meets its first inflation print at 8:30 this morning, and Oracle speaks for the AI trade tonight.
subline: Futures lean higher after three down days, August PPI and jobless claims land at 8:30 with CPI tomorrow, and next week's Fed meeting has a hike in the conversation.
asof: Pre-market · as of 6:50 AM ET · index values are futures · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Stocks fall a third day as oil tops $100
items.sentence: The S&P 500 fell 0.48 percent to 7,636.46, its third straight loss, with energy up 1.1 percent as the only sector to finish higher, per Alain Guillot's market recap.

items.title: Futures lean higher after three down days
items.sentence: S&P 500 futures trade near 7,654, up 0.23 percent, with Dow futures up 0.38 percent and Nasdaq 100 futures flat, per Investing.com's pre-market board.

items.title: PPI at 8:30 today, CPI tomorrow
items.sentence: August producer prices and weekly jobless claims land at 8:30 AM ET with existing-home sales at 10, and the Cleveland Fed's nowcast puts tomorrow's headline CPI near 3.38 percent, per Kiplinger.

items.title: Brent holds $102, its highest since May
items.sentence: Brent trades at $102.01, up 0.79 percent, with WTI at $97.32, as the intensifying US-Iran conflict keeps supply risk in the price, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Gold sits tight at $4,398
items.sentence: Gold is little changed at $4,398 an ounce after briefly topping $4,400, still up 21 percent over the past year, as traders wait on the inflation prints, per Trading Economics.

items.title: The 10-year at 4.85%, a three-year high
items.sentence: The 10-year yield sits at 4.85 percent, its highest since October 2023, pressured by oil, more than $1.5 trillion of AI-linked corporate borrowing, and a Treasury buyback program tripled to $6 billion, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Bitcoin eases to $77,947
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades at $77,947, down 1.3 percent over 24 hours and about 38 percent below its October 2025 record of $126,080, though roughly flat on the week, per CoinGecko.

items.title: Houthis hit Saudi cities in major escalation
items.sentence: Iran-backed Houthis attacked Saudi cities and Aramco facilities in what CNN calls a major regional escalation, wounding scores and drawing retaliatory Saudi airstrikes.

items.title: US destroys five tankers; Hormuz traffic dwindles
items.sentence: US forces destroyed five IRGC-linked oil tankers after Iranian missile attacks on a Navy warship, Jordan intercepted 18 Iranian missiles, and Strait of Hormuz traffic is running near 10 ships a day against a prewar 130, per CBS News.

items.title: Trump pledges $5,000 checks if GOP holds Congress
items.sentence: President Trump pledged a $5,000 'dividend' to American adults if Republicans keep Congress in November, with no funding mechanism specified yet, per CNBC.

items.title: Gas averages $4.15, up nearly a dollar
items.sentence: Regular gasoline now averages $4.15 a gallon nationally, almost a dollar more than last Labor Day, as the tanker war reaches the pump, per CBS News.

items.title: Meta jumps 6.5% on its Muse agent
items.sentence: Meta closed at $653.69, up 6.55 percent on nearly double its average volume, after Morgan Stanley sized the AI-agent market Muse is chasing at roughly $30 trillion, per The Motley Fool.

items.title: Apple's new CEO unveils the foldable iPhone Duo
items.sentence: John Ternus used his first product keynote as chief executive to introduce the iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable, alongside the iPhone 18 line, per NPR.

items.title: Oracle reports tonight; $638 billion backlog in focus
items.sentence: Oracle reports fiscal first-quarter results after today's close with its $638 billion AI backlog the number Wall Street cares about, and Adobe reports the same day, per InvestingLive.

items.title: California signs first-in-nation AI auditor law
items.sentence: Governor Newsom signed first-in-the-nation legislation, anchored by SB 813, creating a registry of independent AI auditors and standards for safety evaluations, per the governor's office.

items.title: OpenAI and Samsung pair up on chips
items.sentence: OpenAI is partnering with Samsung on next-generation AI chip development, adding another leg to its compute buildout, per AI Weekly's roundup of Wednesday's announcements.
